svg.title: Agent loop: from call-out to verified day
svg.desc: Second Shift agent loop: 1 Slack call-out, 2 LLM reads who and when, 3 guardrails, 4 read Sheets and Calendar and fingerprint, 5 CP-SAT re-plan, 6 independent rule check, 7 dispatcher approves, 8 re-read and compare fingerprint, 9 ledger writes in order, 10 read back and rule check.
svg.text: Agent loop: from call-out to verified day
Second Shift. Follow the numbers. Box color shows who does the work.
A tech posts in #dispatch: "out sick today".
Or dispatch asks: "what if Wei doesn't show up?"
Strict schema: which tech, which hours, how sure,
and whether it is real or a what-if.
Checks the model's answer. Never guesses who is out.
Outcomes: ignore | ask | plan | simulate what-if
Jobs, skills, windows, drive times. One calendar per
tech is the schedule of record, plus busy blocks.
Skills, equipment, arrival windows, shifts, drive time.
Urgent first. Bump only for more urgent. Fewest changes.
A separate checker re-verifies every rule
on the proposed plan before anyone sees it.
Reviews the plan in the web dashboard.
Same Sheets and Calendar as when the plan was made?
Match: go on and write. Changed: stop.
Re-read Calendar, Sheets, Slack and Gmail.
Run the rule checker on the real calendars.
Write through the ledger, in this order
Every write is logged: pending, then done or failed. Calendar event ids are fixed per plan.
Slack and Gmail sends are keyed and looked up before any retry. Retries back off.
After a crash it resumes where it stopped. A second approve changes nothing.
Unsure who or when: ask in Slack.
A rule broke, or no valid plan.
Nothing written. Slack gets the impact.
Dashboard shows it with "Make it real".
The model is called once, at step 2. Every later step is plain code or a person.
Demo day: 3 of Marco's 4 jobs covered
by a chain move. Greedy baseline: 1 of 4.
